title: Every state-mutating HTTP endpoint must declare its error contract enumerating all failure modes a client can observe
statement: Every implemented endpoint with HTTP method in `{POST, PATCH, PUT, DELETE}` MUST declare an error contract enumerating every distinct response the caller can observe, keyed by `{statusCode, errorCode, retriability}`. The contract may be a sibling `*.errors.json` file under `docs/framework/contracts/`, a discoverable `@ApiResponse` decorator chain, or use-case `alternateFlows[]` documentation. The minimum set includes validation, authorization, not-found, applicable conflict, and applicable rate-limit failures. An undocumented mutating endpoint is a release-gating finding.
rationale: Stynx's `StynxErrorFilter` (in `@stynx-nyx/core`) translates exceptions into stable error response shapes, and adopters get consistent error envelopes for free — but pre-Phase-30 no invariant required adopters to *document* which exceptions each endpoint can throw. `sense-spec-robustness-targets` (Phase 27.E) flagged stynx FAIL on F1×T8 because zero invariants were typed `error_semantics`. This invariant promotes a baseline gate scoped to mutations (write endpoints have the highest impact when a client can't predict failure modes — silent retries can corrupt state). Adopters who use NestJS's `@ApiResponse` decorators get most of this for free; the gate forces the documentation discipline. Conservative scope (mutations only) keeps the initial promotion tractable — read-endpoint error contracts can land as INV-ERROR-002 if/when needed.
